newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses end mixed,wary of US uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses end mixed,wary of US uncertainty.

text.p: European bourses ended the day mixed on Friday with investors wary ahead of important U.S. economic indicators due on Friday and American elections next week.
On currency markets, the dollar strengthened against the mark in late trading and regained some losses on the yen. Jitters before next week's U.S. election caused profit-taking earlier.

London and Paris bourses perked up strongly as U.S. economic data suggesting the economy may not be growing so fast made for a positive start on Wall Street. But Frankfurt ended well down as hopes of lower German interes rates faded.
London closed up 0.4 percent, clawing back losses in the wake of Wednesday's surprise interest rate increase but the market remained edgy because of uncertainty over Friday's U.S. figures.
Traders said activity had been subdued and the mood was cautious ahead of the potentially market-moving U.S. jobs data which would give signals on inflationaty pressures in the United States.
London recovered as some investors saw signs of subdued inflation in U.S. data on Thursday showing higher-than-expected weekly jobless claims and weaker-than-expected spending data.
But trading was thin and Wall Street's recent volatility continued to cloud sentiment.

"But I doubt if Wall Street will make much progress," said one trader. "It is much more likely that any action will be on the downside ahead of the payrolls report tomorrow and the elections next week," he added.
French stocks were the best performers, climbing to register a 0.75 percent increease at the close. A small interest rate cut and the U.S. statistics supported the market.
The Bank of France reduced its intervention rate by five basis points to 3.20 percent after its monetary policy council meeting in a move described as cautious by economists.
Frankfurt stocks had a bad day, closing down 0.7 percent after thin trading. Dealers said the market was weak as expectation of further German rate cuts faded after the British hike.
The dollar made up lost ground against the mark in late European trading but remained slightly weaker against the yen

"The dollar is once again in a pattern defined by solid support on the downside and difficulty in overcoming resistance on the upside, which is keeping it in a neutral mode," said Teis Knuthsen, international economist at First Chicago in London.
Against the yen, the dollar ended at 113.77 yen, up from a Far Eastern low at around 113.20 but slightly down on the levels seen in late European trading on Wednesday.

While the dollar looks set to remain stuck in a narrow range against the mark, traders were confident the dollar's slide against the yen was a blip in a healthy trend that has carried it to 42-month highs against the Japanese currency.
An eleventh-hour attack of nerves ahead of next week's U.S. election sparked overnight profit-taking on the dollar.

"The main driving force behind this currency pair is Japanese investors and their need to invest abroad to enhance yield, and we see this continuing," said Stuart Thomson, chief international economist at Nikko Europe in London.
Analysts said the market was fearful U.S. Democrats would seize control of Congress on November 5, ushering in an era of looser fiscal and trade policy.
CURRENCIES AT 1700
The dollar was trading around 1.5132 marks and 113.77 yen versus 1.5095 and 113.89 in late European business on Wednesday.
STOCKS CLOSING PRICES
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 15.2 points higher at 3,979.1.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 15.75 at 2,140.51.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 19.48 at 2,659.25.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended lower at $379.75 an ounce, compared with $380.05 at Wednesday's close. Silver closed three cents higher at $4.86.
